mainTopic: The כוס של ברכה, the sources and text of night and daytime קידוש, and the time limit for making up a missed הבדלה.
overview: This amud finishes a list of 'שמע מינה' lessons from a ברייתא about the כוס של ברכה. One cup can serve for two קדושות, and the ברייתא follows בית שמאי as רבי יהודה reports them. רב אשי says that טעמו פגמו is really the same lesson as the rule that the cup needs a שיעור, and three אמוראים were personally stricter about 'blemished' wine. Next, a ברייתא learns קידוש over wine from 'זכור את יום השבת'. The גמרא re-reads it so that the main קידוש is at night, and a second, daytime קידוש comes from the word 'day'. רב יהודה rules that the daytime קידוש is just בורא פרי הגפן, and a story about רב אשי in מחוזא shows this. Finally, the גמרא sets the time for a missed הבדלה: it can be made up until Wednesday, because the first three days count as 'after שבת', but without the ברכה on fire. The amud ends as רב ברונא begins a teaching in the name of רב, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Two sanctifications may be said over one cup
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא continues its list of lessons from the ברייתא: one cup of wine can be used for two separate קדושות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And learn from it: a person may say two sanctifications over one cup.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is adding another lesson to its ongoing list of things we learn from the ברייתא. This one says that a single cup can carry two separate blessings of sanctification.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, someone with only one cup uses it for more than one ברכה, such as ברכת המזון and הבדלה. From this the גמרא learns that one cup can carry two separate קדושות. We do not need a separate cup for each one.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it. This introduces a lesson drawn from a source.
Sanctifications, meaning blessings of holiness such as קידוש or הבדלה.

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a practical rule. Someone with only one cup of wine can still fulfill more than one ברכה with it.

phrases.english: And learn from it:
phrases.notes: Continues a list of inferences from the ברייתא that began on the previous amud.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹמֵר שְׁתֵּי קְדוּשּׁוֹת עַל כּוֹס אֶחָד.
phrases.english: one recites two sanctifications over one cup.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמַע מִינַּהּ: אוֹמֵר שְׁתֵּי קְדוּשּׁוֹת עַל כּוֹס אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of שמע מינה inferences from the ברייתא that began on the previous part of the daf.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: One cup can serve for two separate קדושות.

steps.title: The ברייתא follows בית שמאי as explained by רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The final inference: the ברייתא follows the view of בית שמאי as רבי יהודה reports it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And learn from it: this ברייתא is following בית שמאי, according to רבי יהודה's version of their view.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws one more lesson. It identifies whose opinion the ברייתא follows: בית שמאי, as רבי יהודה explains them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי and בית הלל disagree about the order of the ברכות said over the cup, and תנאים report that disagreement in different ways. The order in this ברייתא matches only רבי יהודה's report of בית שמאי's view, so the ברייתא must follow that opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: According to רבי יהודה, meaning his report of the dispute.

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean רבי יהודה himself holds like בית שמאי. It means the ברייתא follows בית שמאי's view as רבי יהודה reports that view.

phrases.english: And learn from it:
it is the view of Beit Shammai,
and according to Rabbi Yehuda's version.
phrases.notes: רבי יהודה reports a specific version of the dispute between בית שמאי and בית הלל.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמַע מִינַּהּ: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי הִיא, וְאַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The last item in the list of inferences.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ברייתא follows בית שמאי's view as רבי יהודה reports it.

steps.title: רב אשי: two of the lessons are really one
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי objects to counting טעמו פגמו and כוס של ברכה צריך שיעור as two separate lessons. He says they are one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: 'Tasting it ruins it' and 'a cup of blessing needs a minimum amount' are one single idea.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי steps in to correct the list. He says two of the lessons counted earlier should not be counted separately, because they are one idea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier list treated 'tasting ruins the cup' and 'a cup of blessing needs a minimum amount' as two independent rules. רב אשי says they are one rule. He will explain how in the next line.

keyTerms.meaning: If he tasted it, he blemished it. The cup is now ruined for a ברכה.
A cup of blessing, the wine used for קידוש, הבדלה, or ברכת המזון.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
'If he tasted it he blemished it'
and 'a cup of blessing requires a measure' —
are one matter.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: טְעָמוֹ פְּגָמוֹ וְכוֹס שֶׁל בְּרָכָה צָרִיךְ שִׁיעוּר — חֲדָא מִילְּתָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the earlier list of inferences and rejects counting two of them separately.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the counting of two inferences as separate. Both rules themselves are accepted.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The list double-counts one idea as two lessons.

steps.title: Tasting ruins the cup only because it lowers the amount
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains that tasting ruins the cup because a cup of blessing needs a minimum amount, and tasting reduces it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is what it means: why does tasting ruin the cup? Because a cup of blessing needs a minimum amount.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי explains how the two lessons are really one. Tasting ruins the cup only because it can leave less wine than the minimum required amount.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, one could think the act of sipping makes the wine unfit by itself. רב אשי says the only problem is the amount. So if enough wine is still left after a sip, the cup can still be used for a ברכה.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is what it is saying. This introduces a reinterpretation.

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב אשי, tasting the cup is not a problem in itself. The only issue is whether the minimum amount of wine is still in the cup.
steps.confusionAlert: The question 'מאי טעמא' here is not a challenge. רב אשי is asking it to set up his own explanation.
steps.whyThisMatters: This has a practical result. A cup that was sipped from but still holds the minimum amount is still usable for a ברכה.

phrases.english: And this is what it is saying:
What is the reason that tasting it blemishes it?

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם דְּכוֹס שֶׁל בְּרָכָה צָרִיךְ שִׁיעוּר.
phrases.english: Because a cup of blessing requires a measure.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָכִי קָאָמַר: מַאי טַעְמָא טְעָמוֹ פְּגָמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the claim רב אשי made in the previous step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Tasting ruins a cup of blessing only because it reduces the wine below the required minimum amount.

steps.title: Three אמוראים who were strict about blemished wine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reports that three אמוראים each avoided wine that had been 'blemished,' each at a different level: a pitcher, a cup, or even a barrel.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יעקב בר אידי was careful about a pitcher someone had drunk from. רב אידי בר שישא was careful about a cup someone had drunk from. מר בר רב אשי was careful even about a barrel that had already been opened and used.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells us how three אמוראים acted in practice. Each one refused to use 'blemished' wine for a ברכה, and each drew the line in a different place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These are personal stringencies that go beyond רב אשי's basic rule. רבי יעקב בר אידי avoided wine from a pitcher that had been drunk from. רב אידי בר שישא avoided a cup that had been drunk from, and מר בר רב אשי went furthest by avoiding wine from an already opened barrel.

keyTerms.meaning: Was particular or strict about something.
Blemished, meaning already drunk from or used.

steps.whatToRemember: רב אשי's basic rule is that only the amount matters. Even so, some אמוראים chose to be stricter and used only wine that had not been 'blemished' at all.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ya'akov bar Idi
was particular about a blemished pitcher.
Rav Idi bar Sheisha
was particular about a blemished cup.
Mar bar Rav Ashi
was particular even about a blemished barrel.
phrases.notes: He used wine only from a barrel that had not yet been opened.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב בַּר אִידִי קָפֵיד אַחַצְבָּא פְּגִימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the basic rule about blemished cups, the גמרא shows how some אמוראים were stricter in practice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Some אמוראים were strict about blemished wine at the level of the pitcher, the cup, or even the barrel.

steps.title: A ברייתא: remember שבת over wine, by day and by night
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns קידוש on wine from 'זכור את יום השבת לקדשו'. It treats day as the obvious case and asks for the source for night.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: 'Remember the day of שבת to make it holy' means remember it over wine. I only know this for the daytime. How do I know it applies at night? The verse says: 'Remember the day of שבת to make it holy.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that uses the פסוק of זכור to require קידוש over wine. As the text is written, it seems to say the daytime is the obvious case and the night needs a separate source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא reads the word זכור as a command to say קידוש over a cup of wine. It then follows a common pattern, 'I only know X, from where do I know Y?', with day as X and night as Y. That order is exactly what the גמרא is about to question.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages taught: this introduces a ברייתא
Remember: the source word for קידוש
I only know [this case]: a standard derivation formula
The verse teaches: this introduces the proof verse

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
'Remember the day of Shabbat to sanctify it'
remember it over wine.
I only have [this] for the daytime;
from where [do we know] at night?

phrases.aramaic: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״זָכוֹר אֶת יוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת לְקַדְּשׁוֹ״.
phrases.english: The verse teaches: 'Remember the day of Shabbat to sanctify it.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: the scriptural source of קידוש on wine, moving on from the wine-related lessons of the earlier steps.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק of זכור requires remembering שבת over wine. As written, day is the base case and night is derived.

steps.title: Challenge: night is the main time for קידוש
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא is surprised that the ברייתא asks for a night source. Night is the main קידוש, because you sanctify the day at its beginning.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'From where do we know at night'?! Just the opposite! The main קידוש is said at night, because when you sanctify a day, you must sanctify it at its beginning!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the order of the ברייתא. It should not be asking for a source for night, since night is the main time for קידוש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Making a day holy belongs at its start, which is Friday night. So night is the obvious, main case. Treating it as the extra case that needs a special source seems backwards.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary: the opposite is true

steps.confusionAlert: Remember that a Jewish day begins at night. 'The beginning of the day' here means Friday night, not שבת morning.

phrases.english: 'From where [do we know] at night'?!
On the contrary, the main Kiddush
is sanctified at night,
for when one sanctifies,
one must sanctify the beginning of the day!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the order of the derivation in the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's treatment of night קידוש as the case that needs a derivation
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Sanctifying a day belongs at its start, so night is the primary קידוש and should be the base case, not the derived one.

steps.title: Second challenge: a 'day' verse is used to prove night
steps.stepSummary: A further difficulty: the ברייתא looks for a source for night, yet quotes a פסוק that says 'day'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore: 'From where do we know at night? The verse says: Remember the day.' The תנא is searching for a source for night, and he brings a verse about the day?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second problem with the ברייתא as written. The proof verse it brings for night speaks about the 'day'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Proving night קידוש from the word יום (day) makes no sense on its face. Together with the first challenge, this shows that the ברייתא must be read differently.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore: this adds another difficulty

phrases.english: And furthermore:
'From where [do we know] at night?
The verse teaches: Remember the day,'
the תנא is searching for [a source for] night
and he takes a verse about the day?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second challenge against the same wording.
steps.kashyaTarget: The proof verse that the ברייתא cites for night
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A verse that says 'day' cannot be the source for a night obligation.

steps.title: Corrected reading: night is the base case and day is derived
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא re-reads the ברייתא. זכור means קידוש at the start of שבת, and the word 'day' adds daytime קידוש.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it means: 'Remember the day of שבת to make it holy' means remember it over wine when שבת comes in. I only know this for the night. How do I know it applies during the day? The verse says: 'Remember the DAY of שבת.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers both challenges by flipping the order of the ברייתא. Night is the main קידוש, and daytime is the extra one learned from the word 'day'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With this reading, the first challenge disappears because night is now the base case ('when שבת comes in'). The second challenge disappears too, because the verse with 'day' is now used to prove daytime קידוש.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means: introduces a re-reading of the text
When it enters, at the start of שבת

steps.whatToRemember: Main קידוש is on Friday night, when שבת begins. A second, daytime קידוש is learned from the word יום in the פסוק.

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
'Remember the day of Shabbat to sanctify it':
remember it over wine when it enters;
I only have [this] at night;
from where [do we know] during the day?
The verse teaches: 'Remember the day of Shabbat.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves both challenges by re-reading the ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Day is the base case and night is derived from the verse.
steps.terutzMaskana: Night (at the entry of שבת) is the base case, and daytime קידוש is derived from the word 'day'.

steps.title: What blessing is said for daytime קידוש?
steps.stepSummary: Now that there is a daytime קידוש, the גמרא asks which ברכה is said for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: During the day, what ברכה does one say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a practical follow-up question about the daytime קידוש it just established.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The night קידוש has a full ברכה about the holiness of שבת. The question is whether the daytime version needs its own special text.

phrases.english: During the day, what blessing does one recite?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A practical follow-up to the daytime קידוש derived in Step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The text of the ברכה for daytime קידוש

steps.title: רב יהודה: just בורא פרי הגפן
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה says that daytime קידוש is simply the ברכה on wine, בורא פרי הגפן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: 'Who creates the fruit of the vine.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers that there is no special text for daytime קידוש. You simply say the normal ברכה on wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The daytime קידוש is only a 'remembering' over wine. It is not a second full sanctification of the day, so the wine ברכה alone is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: Who creates the fruit of the vine: the ברכה on wine

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
'Who creates the fruit of the vine.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Daytime קידוש is just בורא פרי הגפן.

steps.title: רב אשי in מחוזא is asked to make the 'great קידוש'
steps.stepSummary: A story begins: רב אשי visits מחוזא, and the people ask him to say the 'קידושא רבה' and bring him wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי came to מחוזא. They said to him: 'Let the master make for us the great קידוש.' (They gave him [a cup].)
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story that illustrates daytime קידוש. This line is setup, and the story continues in the next part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The people of מחוזא call the daytime קידוש by a grand name, 'the great קידוש'. This creates suspense: does it have some special long text? The rest of the story will show what רב אשי actually did.

keyTerms.meaning: The great קידוש: a name for daytime קידוש
They gave him [a cup of wine]

steps.confusionAlert: Despite the name 'great קידוש,' the daytime קידוש is the simpler one. The name does not mean it is longer than Friday night's.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi happened to come to Mechoza;
they said to him:
Let the master sanctify for us
the great Kiddush.
(They gave him [a cup].)

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a story that will illustrate רב יהודה's ruling about daytime קידוש.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Setup: the people of מחוזא ask רב אשי to make the daytime 'great קידוש'. The resolution follows in the continuation of the story.

steps.title: רב אשי wonders what the 'great קידוש' is
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי asks himself what the people of מחוזא mean by 'קידושא רבה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: He thought: What is this 'great קידוש'?
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues. רב אשי is unsure what the people mean by 'קידושא רבה', so he asks himself what it is. This sets up his next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The name 'great קידוש' sounds as if it should contain a long, special text. רב אשי does not know whether the people of מחוזא expect extra ברכות. His private question creates the suspense that the story will soon resolve.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The great קידוש', a name for the daytime קידוש

phrases.english: He thought: What is this 'great kiddush'?
phrases.notes: An internal question. רב אשי is thinking, not speaking out loud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story from Step 12, where the people asked רב אשי to say the 'קידושא רבה'.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What text the 'great קידוש' actually contains.

steps.title: רב אשי starts with the wine blessing and draws it out
steps.stepSummary: Since every ברכה said over wine begins with בורא פרי הגפן, רב אשי says it and stretches it out.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to himself: Since with all ברכות said over wine, people say בורא פרי הגפן first, I will start there. He said בורא פרי הגפן and drew it out.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי reasons that whatever else might come, בורא פרי הגפן always comes first. So he says it, and he says it slowly to see whether the people expect more.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a clever safe move. Starting with the wine ברכה is correct no matter what follows. Drawing it out gives him time to watch how the people react.

keyTerms.meaning: And he drew it out (said it slowly and at length)

phrases.english: He said: Since with all the blessings,
phrases.notes: This means all ברכות that are said over a cup of wine.

phrases.english: they say 'Who creates the fruit of the vine' first,
he said 'Who creates the fruit of the vine' and drew it out.
phrases.notes: He lengthened the ברכה to wait and see whether more was expected.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב אשי answers his own question in a practical way. He begins with the one ברכה he knows is certainly part of it.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Begin with בורא פרי הגפן, since it always comes first, and see whether more is expected.

steps.title: An elder drinks, showing the great קידוש was just the wine blessing
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי sees an old man drinking and understands that the 'great קידוש' was only בורא פרי הגפן. He praises his own alertness with a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: He saw a certain old man bend over and drink. He applied to himself the פסוק: 'The wise man has his eyes in his head.'
steps.whatsHappening: Right after the wine ברכה, an elder drinks. That shows רב אשי the 'great קידוש' was already finished. He applies a פסוק to himself, praising the wise person who keeps his eyes open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fancy name turns out to mean just the wine ברכה. This story supports רב יהודה's rule from Step 11 that daytime קידוש is simply בורא פרי הגפן. The פסוק is about being alert enough to read the situation.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The wise man has his eyes in his head' (קהלת ב:יד)

steps.whatToRemember: The daytime 'קידושא רבה' is just בורא פרי הגפן. The story of רב אשי in מחוזא shows this rule in action and supports רב יהודה.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not be fooled by the name 'great קידוש'. Despite the name, it is the simplest קידוש, just the ברכה on wine.

phrases.english: He saw a certain old man bending over and drinking,
phrases.notes: Drinking showed that the קידוש was over.

phrases.english: he applied to himself: 'The wise man, his eyes are in his head.'
phrases.notes: קהלת ב:יד. The wise person stays alert and notices what is going on.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the story and confirms that nothing more was expected after the wine ברכה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The daytime קידוש consists only of בורא פרי הגפן, as רב יהודה said.

steps.title: One who missed הבדלה can make it during the week
steps.stepSummary: בני רבי חייא rule that someone who did not make הבדלה on מוצאי שבת can still make it later in the week.
steps.simpleTranslation: The sons of רבי חייא say: Someone who did not make הבדלה on מוצאי שבת may make it any time during the whole week.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic: a person who forgot or missed הבדלה. בני רבי חייא say he can make it up later in the week.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here הבדלה is not tied only to מוצאי שבת. It can still be made up afterward. The phrase 'the whole week' is broad and invites the next question about how long this really lasts.
steps.confusionAlert: In this line, 'הַשַּׁבָּת כּוּלּוֹ' means 'the whole week', not 'all of שבת'. In the language of חז"ל, the word שבת can mean the week.

phrases.english: The sons of Rabbi Chiya say:
One who did not make havdala at the end of Shabbat
may make havdala throughout the entire week.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא leaves daytime קידוש and returns to a statement of בני רבי חייא that was quoted earlier in the סוגיא, now to discuss making up a missed הבדלה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A missed הבדלה may be made up later in the week.

steps.title: Until when can late הבדלה be made
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how many days into the week a person can still make הבדלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And until how long?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the exact limit. Does 'the whole week' really mean all of it? This question sets up רבי זירא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling of בני רבי חייא gave no clear end point. The גמרא wants to know exactly when the chance to make הבדלה runs out.

keyTerms.meaning: And until how much / how long?

phrases.english: And until how long?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the exact time limit of the ruling in Step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The last day on which late הבדלה may still be made.

steps.title: רבי זירא: until Wednesday
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא says late הבדלה may be made until the fourth day of the week.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: Until the fourth day of the week.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא gives the limit: until רביעי בשבת, the fourth day of the week. Practically, this means up through Tuesday, before Wednesday.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though the ruling said 'the whole week', the time for הבדלה really lasts only while the days still count as 'after שבת'. From Wednesday on, the days count as belonging to the coming שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: The fourth day of the week (Wednesday)

steps.confusionAlert: 'עד רביעי' means up until Wednesday, not including it. The next step's parallel shows that Wednesday already counts as 'before שבת'.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: עַד רְבִיעִי בְּשַׁבָּת.
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said: Until the fourth day of the week.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: עַד רְבִיעִי בְּשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Late הבדלה may be made until the fourth day of the week.

steps.title: Parallel from גיטין: the first three days count as after שבת
steps.stepSummary: A rule about the wording of גיטין supports רבי זירא. Sunday through Tuesday count as 'after שבת', and Wednesday through Friday count as 'before שבת'.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like what happened when רבי זירא sat before רב אסי (and some say רב אסי sat before רבי יוחנן). He sat and said: Regarding גיטין, Sunday, Monday, and Tuesday are called 'after שבת'. Wednesday, Thursday, and ערב שבת are called 'before שבת'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up רבי זירא with a matching rule from the laws of גיטין. When a document says 'after שבת', it means the first three days of the week.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The week is split in half: the first three days belong to the past שבת, and the last three belong to the coming שבת. הבדלה separates us from the שבת that just ended. So it can only be made while we are still in the 'after שבת' days, which is why the limit is before Wednesday.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say (a different version of who said it)
The eve of the day, meaning ערב שבת (Friday)

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a key idea: the week is split into 'after the last שבת' and 'before the next שבת'. That split sets the time limit for late הבדלה, and the same split is used in the laws of גיטין.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הָא דְּיָתֵיב רַבִּי זֵירָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב אַסִּי,
phrases.english: Like that time when Rabbi Zeira sat before Rav Asi,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ רַב אַסִּי קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן,
phrases.english: and some say it was Rav Asi before Rabbi Yochanan,
phrases.notes: Two versions of who sat before whom.

phrases.english: and he sat and said: Regarding divorce documents,

phrases.aramaic: חֲדָא בְּשַׁבְּתָא תְּרֵי וּתְלָתָא — בָּתַר שַׁבְּתָא.
phrases.english: Sunday, Monday, and Tuesday are 'after Shabbat.'

phrases.aramaic: אַרְבַּע וְחַמְשָׁא וּמַעֲלֵי יוֹמָא — קַמֵּי שַׁבְּתָא.
phrases.english: Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday are 'before Shabbat.'
phrases.notes: מעלי יומא here means ערב שבת.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הָא דְּיָתֵיב רַבִּי זֵירָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב אַסִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי זירא's limit in Step 18 with a parallel rule about how the week is divided.
steps.raayaObject: רבי זירא's rule that late הבדלה lasts only until Wednesday.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The rule for גיטין that the first three days of the week count as 'after שבת'.

steps.title: Late הבדלה leaves out the blessing over fire
steps.stepSummary: רבי יעקב בר אידי says that a late הבדלה made during the week does not include the ברכה over fire.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יעקב בר אידי said: But not over the fire.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יעקב בר אידי adds a limit. A person may make a late הבדלה during the week, but he does not say the ברכה on fire (בורא מאורי האש).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברכה on fire is connected specifically to מוצאי שבת, when fire was first created. So it is said only then. The rest of הבדלה can still be made up later, but this one part cannot.

keyTerms.meaning: רבי יעקב בר אידי, an אמורא
The fire (the ברכה בורא מאורי האש)

steps.whatToRemember: A missed הבדלה can be made up until Wednesday, because the first three days still count as 'after שבת'. However, the ברכה on fire is said only on מוצאי שבת itself.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yaakov bar Idi said:
But not over the fire.
phrases.notes: No ברכה over fire when making a late הבדלה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב בַּר אִידִי: אֲבָל לֹא עַל הָאוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the late-הבדלה rule of Steps 16 and 18 by removing the ברכה on fire.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A late הבדלה during the week is made without the ברכה over fire.

steps.title: רב ברונא introduces a teaching in the name of רב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new statement. רב ברונא reports a teaching that he received from רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ברונא said that רב said:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move by naming the speaker of a new ruling. The ruling itself comes right after this line, in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line belongs to the statement that follows it and should not be read as a complete step by itself. It shows a chain of tradition: רב ברונא, a student, repeats what his teacher רב taught. Naming the source tells us how much weight the coming rule carries, because it goes back to רב, one of the great early אמוראים.

keyTerms.meaning: Said. This word opens a teaching that is reported in someone's name.
An אמורא and student of רב who passes on his teacher's rulings.
One of the great early אמוראים of Babylonia, whose rulings carry great authority.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not look for a ruling in this line. It only tells you who is speaking. The actual rule comes right after it.

phrases.english: Rav Beruna said
phrases.notes: Names the person who is reporting the teaching.

phrases.english: Rav said:
phrases.notes: Names the original source of the teaching. The colon shows that the content follows next.

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: Attribution formula that opens the next מימרא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבי יעקב בר אידי's rule about late הבדלה, the גמרא introduces a new ruling from רב ברונא in the name of רב. The ruling continues the discussion of the laws of the שבת meal and its blessings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Not yet stated. This line only gives the attribution, and the ruling follows on the next amud.
